ties.basis: 025-1b-LE-006.krn lines 341/350: source tie continues in another encoded voice of the same staff; LilyPond cannot tie across voices, so the note is held, not reattacked.

bars.description: Bars 1-63 once in written order. The source has no repeat signs; nothing is cut or repeated.

endpoints.basis: MEAS, cached pitch features (dB re the 95th-percentile total). First: the opening B4/D-sharp5 trill in thirds (MIDI 71/75) rises from about -44 to -17 dB at 2.60-2.65 s; a broad 0-4 s window had chosen 3.62 s, a later trill attack. Last: in this acoustic transfer the bass of the final G-sharp-major chord (q248) is below the surface-noise floor; its rolled upper notes rise at G-sharp3 (56) 116.0 s, C4 (60) 116.6 s, D-sharp4 (63) 116.8 s and C5 (72) 117.0 s. The window [115.88, 116.02] takes the first measurable chord note (a wider 115.9-116.15 window measured 116.14 s, on a later D-sharp4 swell); the bass attack itself is not measured. Periodic surface clicks every 0.77 s (one 78-rpm revolution) continue after the music.

Edition: the Paris edition of Études Op. 25 catalogued by NIFC Chopin First Editions Online as 025-1b-LE-006, publisher recorded in the file as Lemoine, Paris (RISM 1001002392, PL-Wbfc 4808/n); encoding Marta Lawrence, editing Wojciech Jakubiak-Danek and Mateusz Mrugas. The performer's edition is not established; first-edition readings can differ from later editions.

Conversion: tools/align/humdrum_convert.py reads the unchanged **kern tokens (Humdrum line timing, spine splits/merges, explicit sounding pitches, ties, graces, tuplets) and writes plain MusicXML for the pinned LilyPond 2.24.4 converter. Dynamics, hairpins, pedalling, fingering, stems, layout comments, *rscale display scaling, cue size and editorial text are not converted; slurs are kept only when both ends lie in one encoded voice. Voices are the encoded Humdrum sub-spines on each staff (MusicXML voices 1-4 upper, 5-8 lower), labelled here only as upper/lower staff.

Source identity (MEAS): the compiled events match all 2,550 regular **kern attacks (tied continuations excluded) by pitch within one MIDI tick (maximum onset difference 0.0 quarter), plus the single grace note. Independent check with Verovio 6.3.0's Humdrum importer: 2,553 notes in both readings; per-measure relative timing agrees in all 63 measures.
One source tie continues in a different encoded voice (F-sharp5 into bar 16, lines 341/350); extraction.ties holds it as one event. The engraving may show that tie arc as unterminated.

Recording: Ignacy Jan Paderewski, Victor 917-B (matrix B-27918, take 1), 4 May 1923 (content/listen module). Acoustic transfer: the tuning estimate is 445.88 Hz (+23 cents, plausibly transfer speed); energy below about G2 is not measurable, so bass attacks are not individually measured and periodic 78-rpm surface clicks are present.

anchors.label: bar-61-C-sharp2-chord
anchors.basis: MEAS: the bar-61 second chord C-sharp2/G-sharp2/E3/G-sharp3/A-sharp3 (q242), measured on its upper notes. MEAS band energies (dB re the 95th-percentile total; this acoustic transfer has no measurable energy below about G2, so bass notes are not measured): A-sharp3/G-sharp3 (58/56) jump at 110.55-110.7 s (-31.8 to -12.8 dB) after near-silence at 110.2-110.5 s; C4/D-sharp3 (60/51) rise at 111.6-111.8 s; the rolled q246 chord enters G3 (55) 113.30-113.40 s, C-sharp4 (61) 113.55-113.60, D-sharp4 (63) 113.80-113.85 and A-sharp4 (70) 114.05-114.10 s. A D-sharp4 re-attack at 115.25 s has no written counterpart. Surface clicks recur every 0.77 s (113.7, 114.45, 115.2, 116.0 s ...); the measured rises are single-pitch, sustained increases, not broadband clicks.
